title.en: From cotton boll to your shirt

text.en: Your shirt started as cotton in a field, became yarn in a spinning mill and cloth in a weaving unit. Manufacturing turns raw material into goods of higher value.

Manufacturing is the production of goods in large quantities after processing raw material into more valuable products. It is called the backbone of development.
Industries help agriculture, create jobs and bring in foreign exchange through exports, and reduce poverty and unemployment.
Industries are classified by raw material into agro-based and mineral-based, by role into basic and consumer, by capital into small and large, and by ownership into public, private, joint and co-operative.
Cotton textiles is a major agro-based industry. Spinning is centred in the cotton belt and weaving is decentralised. India is a leading producer of yarn.
Jute, sugar and silk are other agro-based industries. Sugar mills are shifting to the south and west because cane there has a higher sucrose content.
The iron and steel industry is the basic industry. It needs iron ore, coking coal and limestone, and Bhilai in Chhattisgarh is a public sector steel plant. Jamshedpur, Durgapur, Rourkela and Salem are other well-known centres (additional, not in the textbook).
Other industries include aluminium smelting, chemicals, fertiliser, cement, automobile and information technology.
Industries cause air, water, land and noise pollution. Pollution can be reduced by treating waste and using cleaner technologies.

problem.en: A mill makes 200 shirts a day and each earns Rs 50 profit. What is the profit in 10 days?

prompt.en: Why is manufacturing the backbone of development?

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking farming has no link to industry

points.en: Manufacturing adds value and creates jobs.
Industries can be grouped by raw material, role, capital and ownership.
Steel needs iron ore, coking coal and limestone.
